name: top-1m-domains (PeterDaveHello)
what_it_holds: Curated list of download links (not committed data) to eight top-domain ranking services: Alexa (historical), Cisco Umbrella, Majestic, BuiltWith, Statvoo, DomCop, Tranco, and Cloudflare Radar top domains — mostly .csv.zip direct-download URLs to each vendor's own host.
why_useful: One-stop index of where to pull Tranco/Majestic/Cisco Umbrella/Cloudflare top-1M domain CSVs (each free, updated daily/weekly) for building an airbnb.com and competitor-domain rank time series (gap #5) — a navigation aid rather than a dataset itself.
time_coverage: current snapshots only (links point to daily/weekly vendor feeds, not history)
themes: Web-traffic estimates and domain ranks: Similarweb scrapers or samples, Cloudflare Radar API, Chrome UX Report popularity rank, Tranco, Majestic Million, Common Crawl host-graph rank
why_all: One-stop index of where to pull Tranco/Majestic/Cisco Umbrella/Cloudflare top-1M domain CSVs (each free, updated daily/weekly) for building an airbnb.com and competitor-domain rank time series (gap #5) — a navigation aid rather than a dataset itself.

name: pageview-api
what_it_holds: Mature Python client (31 stars, actively updated to Aug 2026) for the official Wikimedia Pageview REST API (per-article, per-project, per-country pageview counts, various access/agent breakdowns). No data committed; it is a well-maintained API wrapper.
why_useful: The most robust, still-maintained Python client for pulling Wikipedia pageviews for any set of city/attraction/company articles going back to mid-2015 (official Wikimedia pageviews dataset start). Fills gap #5 tooling need with a production-quality option rather than a one-off script; could pull ABNB-relevant destination-city pageviews, or even the 'Airbnb' company article itself, as an engagement/interest proxy.
time_coverage: Wikimedia pageviews API covers ~July 2015 to present at daily/monthly/hourly granularity
themes: Wikipedia pageviews tooling and destination-demand datasets (pageviews for cities/attractions as tourism proxies)
Company KPI and alt-data backtest repos for ABNB or OTAs: anyone who already assembled Airbnb quarterly KPI datasets, consensus, or alt-data panels
why_all: The most robust, still-maintained Python client for pulling Wikipedia pageviews for any set of city/attraction/company articles going back to mid-2015 (official Wikimedia pageviews dataset start). Fills gap #5 tooling need with a production-quality option rather than a one-off script; could pull ABNB-relevant destination-city pageviews, or even the 'Airbnb' company article itself, as an engagement/interest proxy.
Directly serves gap #5 (Wikipedia pageviews tooling as an engagement/interest proxy for Airbnb, distinct from the non-point-in-time Google Trends we already tried and found not to work).

name: pageviews (Wikimedia Foundation tool)
what_it_holds: The official-ish, actively maintained (164 stars, updated Sep 2026) Pageviews Analysis web tool used on Wikimedia Toolforge, source code for pageviews.wmcloud.org / pageviews.toolforge.org — lets you compare pageview trends across articles/projects/date ranges interactively, and its underlying code can be adapted to bulk-pull series.
why_useful: Highest-star, best-maintained pageviews tool found in this sweep; even if used only as the live web tool (not cloned), it is the fastest manual way to eyeball a city or attraction's Wikipedia interest trend as a sanity check on other tourism-demand proxies. Its source also documents the API request shape most robustly.
size_hint: web app source, no bundled long time series
themes: Wikipedia pageviews tooling and destination-demand datasets (pageviews for cities/attractions as tourism proxies)
why_all: Highest-star, best-maintained pageviews tool found in this sweep; even if used only as the live web tool (not cloned), it is the fastest manual way to eyeball a city or attraction's Wikipedia interest trend as a sanity check on other tourism-demand proxies. Its source also documents the API request shape most robustly.

Not directly a data source for our pipeline (it is a browser UI, not an API client library to embed), but is the reference implementation showing exactly what pageview granularities/filters (agent type, access method, per-project) are available - useful for spec'ing a pull. Low direct utility since the repo itself is archived and UI-only.

name: wiki-download-parse-page-views
what_it_holds: Python pipeline (GESIS - Leibniz Institute for the Social Sciences) that downloads, filters and aggregates Wikipedia's original hourly/monthly static pagecount dumps from before the 2015 API existed, for a user-specified list of pages and year range, outputting aggregated annual CSV view counts per page. 12 commits; no license file found; notes the dump server throttles to 3 concurrent threads.
why_useful: Another route into the historical raw pageview dumps (2015-present) with an academic-institution maintenance track record, useful as a backup/cross-check to pvduck for building a multi-year destination-pageviews panel.
themes: Wikipedia pageviews tooling and destination-demand datasets (pageviews for cities/attractions as tourism proxies)
why_all: Another route into the historical raw pageview dumps (2015-present) with an academic-institution maintenance track record, useful as a backup/cross-check to pvduck for building a multi-year destination-pageviews panel.

A second, independent route (besides wikipediatrend/statsgrokse) to reconstruct pre-2015 pageview history for any set of destination/city Wikipedia articles directly from Wikimedia's own raw dump archive rather than a third-party mirror — reduces single-point-of-failure risk for the historical-depth use case in Gap 4/5.

name: waxer
what_it_holds: Official Wikimedia R package wrapping the Analytics Query Service (AQS) /metrics REST endpoint (pageviews, unique devices, edits, registered users) for any Wikimedia project. MIT licensed, 24 commits, actively maintained by the Wikimedia Foundation itself.
why_useful: Official, currently-maintained alternative to Commonists/Ironholds for R users wanting AQS/pageviews data; broader than pure pageviews (also edits, unique devices) which could proxy general public attention to a destination or to Airbnb itself.
themes: Wikipedia pageviews tooling and destination-demand datasets (pageviews for cities/attractions as tourism proxies)
why_all: Official, currently-maintained alternative to Commonists/Ironholds for R users wanting AQS/pageviews data; broader than pure pageviews (also edits, unique devices) which could proxy general public attention to a destination or to Airbnb itself.

First-party, presumably most-stable client for the same pageviews API as python-mwviews/pageviews.js, useful if the team's forecasting stack is R-based (the ADR/margin work already uses R-adjacent tooling in places) for pulling destination-article pageviews as an engagement proxy.
